study_area.name: Delhi NCR
study_area.boundary_source: approximate NCR outline (SPEC_v1 §1.2) with Voronoi districts [synthetic]

modes.label: Day · ~10:30 IST
modes.target: Landsat C2 L2 ST (harmonised, 10:45 IST reference)

features.name: ndvi
features.label: NDVI
features.description: Normalised Difference Vegetation Index; denser, greener vegetation cools the surface by transpiration and shading.
features.source: Landsat C2 L2 SR (30 m, TM/ETM+ → OLI harmonised), Apr–Jun median, 1 km mean of fine pixels

features.name: ndbi
features.label: NDBI
features.description: Normalised Difference Built-up Index (SWIR1 vs NIR); high for built-up and bare, dry surfaces.
features.source: Landsat C2 L2 SR (30 m, TM/ETM+ → OLI harmonised), Apr–Jun median, 1 km mean of fine pixels

features.name: mndwi
features.label: MNDWI
features.description: Modified Normalised Difference Water Index (green vs SWIR1); high for open water and wet surfaces.
features.source: Landsat C2 L2 SR (30 m, TM/ETM+ → OLI harmonised), Apr–Jun median, 1 km mean of fine pixels

features.name: albedo
features.label: Albedo
features.description: Broadband shortwave albedo; bright surfaces absorb less solar radiation.
features.source: Landsat C2 L2 SR (30 m, TM/ETM+ → OLI harmonised), Apr–Jun median, 1 km mean of fine pixels (Liang 2001 shortwave albedo)

features.name: ndvi_spring
features.label: NDVI (Feb–Mar)
features.description: Late-winter NDVI, when the rabi crop (wheat, mustard) is green.
features.source: Landsat C2 L2 SR, Feb–Mar median of the frame window

features.name: ndvi_drop
features.label: NDVI drop (spring − season)
features.description: Loss of greenness from Feb–Mar to Apr–Jun; large where crops were harvested and fields lie bare and hot.
features.source: ndvi_spring − ndvi

features.name: frac_built
features.label: Built-up fraction
features.description: Share of the cell covered by buildings and other built-up surfaces.
features.source: JRC GHSL P2023A GHS_BUILT_S, 1 km mean

features.name: frac_forest
features.label: Tree cover
features.description: Share of the cell under trees / forest.
features.source: GLC_FCS30D forest classes on the GHSL simplex

features.name: frac_water
features.label: Water
features.description: Share of the cell covered by open water (rivers, canals, lakes, jheels).
features.source: GLC_FCS30D water on the GHSL simplex

features.name: frac_cropland
features.label: Cropland
features.description: Share of the cell under cultivation.
features.source: GLC_FCS30D cropland on the GHSL simplex

features.name: frac_barren
features.label: Barren land
features.description: Share of the cell that is bare soil, sand or rock.
features.source: GLC_FCS30D bare areas on the GHSL simplex

features.name: built_v
features.label: Built volume (log1p m³/m²)
features.description: Building volume per unit ground area (log); stores daytime heat and releases it at night.
features.source: JRC GHSL P2023A GHS_BUILT_V, 1 km mean

features.name: log_pop
features.label: Population density (log)
features.description: Residents per km² (log); proxy for anthropogenic heat and building density.
features.source: JRC GHSL P2023A GHS_POP, 1 km mean

features.name: dist_urban
features.label: Distance to urban core
features.description: Euclidean distance to the nearest dense urban core.
features.source: derived: distance to cells with 7-cell mean built ≥ 0.5

features.name: dist_builtup
features.label: Distance to built-up
features.description: Euclidean distance to the nearest substantially built-up cell.
features.source: derived: distance to cells with built fraction ≥ 0.3

features.name: lm_pd
features.label: Patch density
features.description: Number of land-cover patches (8-connected) per 100 ha; higher = more fragmented mosaic.
features.source: FRAGSTATS PD on GLC_FCS30D fine land cover

features.name: lm_ed
features.label: Edge density
features.description: Length of boundaries between different land-cover classes per hectare.
features.source: FRAGSTATS ED on GLC_FCS30D fine land cover

features.name: lm_contag
features.label: Contagion
features.description: Aggregation of land-cover classes (0 = maximally interspersed, 100 = one contiguous class).
features.source: FRAGSTATS CONTAG on GLC_FCS30D fine land cover

features.name: dist_water
features.label: Distance to water
features.description: Euclidean distance to the nearest river, canal or lake cell.
features.source: derived: distance to cells with water fraction ≥ 0.3 or JRC water occurrence ≥ 50 %

features.name: elevation
features.label: Elevation
features.description: Mean terrain height; air and surface temperature fall with altitude.
features.source: SRTM GL1 (30 m), cell mean

features.name: slope
features.label: Slope
features.description: Mean terrain slope; steep Aravalli ridges change solar exposure and land use.
features.source: SRTM GL1 (30 m), cell mean

features.name: aspect_sin
features.label: Aspect (east-west)
features.description: Sine of terrain aspect: +1 east-facing, −1 west-facing slopes.
features.source: SRTM GL1, sin(aspect) averaged at 30 m

features.name: aspect_cos
features.label: Aspect (north-south)
features.description: Cosine of terrain aspect: +1 north-facing, −1 south-facing (sun-exposed) slopes.
features.source: SRTM GL1, cos(aspect) averaged at 30 m

features.name: elev_tpi7
features.label: Topographic position (7 km)
features.description: Height above (+) or below (−) the surrounding 7 × 7 cells; valleys collect cold air at night.
features.source: derived: elevation − 7-cell mean

features.name: elev_tpi21
features.label: Topographic position (21 km)
features.description: Height relative to the wider 21 × 21-cell landscape (ridges vs basins).
features.source: derived: elevation − 21-cell mean

features.name: elev_std7
features.label: Relief (7 km std)
features.description: Local relief; high on the Aravalli ridges, ~0 on the Indo-Gangetic plain.
features.source: derived: 7-cell standard deviation of elevation

features.name: era5_t2m
features.label: Air temperature (ERA5-Land)
features.description: Mean 2 m air temperature; carries the regional climate gradient.
features.source: ERA5-Land monthly (Apr–Jun of the frame window), bilinear to 1 km

features.name: era5_vpd
features.label: Vapour-pressure deficit
features.description: Atmospheric drying power; high VPD favours dry, hot surfaces.
features.source: ERA5-Land monthly (Apr–Jun of the frame window), bilinear to 1 km (Magnus formula)

features.name: era5_swvl1
features.label: Soil moisture (0–7 cm)
features.description: Top-soil volumetric water content; wet soils evaporate and warm slowly.
features.source: ERA5-Land monthly (Apr–Jun of the frame window), bilinear to 1 km

features.name: era5_evap
features.label: Evaporation
features.description: Total evaporation; latent heat flux that cools the surface.
features.source: ERA5-Land monthly (Apr–Jun of the frame window), bilinear to 1 km (positive = evaporation)

features.name: era5_ssr
features.label: Net solar radiation
features.description: Surface net shortwave radiation; the energy that heats the surface by day.
features.source: ERA5-Land monthly (Apr–Jun of the frame window), bilinear to 1 km

features.name: era5_wind
features.label: Wind speed
features.description: 10 m wind speed; mixing reduces surface–air temperature contrasts.
features.source: ERA5-Land monthly (Apr–Jun of the frame window), bilinear to 1 km (√(u² + v²) at 10 m)

features.name: era5_precip_jfm
features.label: Winter precipitation (Jan–Mar)
features.description: Antecedent winter rain; recharges soil moisture before the pre-monsoon heat.
features.source: ERA5-Land monthly total precipitation, Jan–Mar of the window years

features.name: ndvi_m3
features.label: NDVI (3-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of NDVI over 3 × 3 cells (6 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 3 × 3-cell box mean of ndvi

features.name: ndvi_m15
features.label: NDVI (15-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of NDVI over 15 × 15 cells (30 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 15 × 15-cell box mean of ndvi

features.name: ndbi_m3
features.label: NDBI (3-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of NDBI over 3 × 3 cells (6 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 3 × 3-cell box mean of ndbi

features.name: ndbi_m15
features.label: NDBI (15-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of NDBI over 15 × 15 cells (30 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 15 × 15-cell box mean of ndbi

features.name: albedo_m3
features.label: Albedo (3-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of Albedo over 3 × 3 cells (6 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 3 × 3-cell box mean of albedo

features.name: albedo_m15
features.label: Albedo (15-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of Albedo over 15 × 15 cells (30 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 15 × 15-cell box mean of albedo

features.name: frac_built_m3
features.label: Built-up fraction (3-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of Built-up fraction over 3 × 3 cells (6 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 3 × 3-cell box mean of frac_built

features.name: frac_built_m15
features.label: Built-up fraction (15-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of Built-up fraction over 15 × 15 cells (30 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 15 × 15-cell box mean of frac_built

features.name: frac_forest_m3
features.label: Tree cover (3-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of Tree cover over 3 × 3 cells (6 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 3 × 3-cell box mean of frac_forest

features.name: frac_forest_m15
features.label: Tree cover (15-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of Tree cover over 15 × 15 cells (30 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 15 × 15-cell box mean of frac_forest

features.name: frac_water_m3
features.label: Water (3-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of Water over 3 × 3 cells (6 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 3 × 3-cell box mean of frac_water

features.name: frac_water_m15
features.label: Water (15-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of Water over 15 × 15 cells (30 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 15 × 15-cell box mean of frac_water

features.name: frac_barren_m3
features.label: Barren land (3-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of Barren land over 3 × 3 cells (6 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 3 × 3-cell box mean of frac_barren

features.name: frac_barren_m15
features.label: Barren land (15-cell mean)
features.description: Neighbourhood mean of Barren land over 15 × 15 cells (30 km); captures the cooling or warming reach of the surrounding land.
features.source: derived: NaN-aware 15 × 15-cell box mean of frac_barren

night.label_caveat: Named Riparian Buffer by the SPEC zone rule, but no cluster shows a riparian signature (mean water 0.7 %); this is the middle-heat cluster of the three non-core zones.

notes: Day LST of the 1990 and 1995 frames comes from Landsat 5 alone: some WRS-2 path/rows have fewer than 6 clear pre-monsoon scenes in the window, so these frames are tiered 'observed-sparse' and are noisier.
The 2005 day frame includes Landsat 7 ETM+ scenes after the 2003 scan-line-corrector failure (SLC-off): striped gaps are filled only by other scenes of the window.

Day LST is a ~10:30 IST snapshot; frames are corrected to a common 10:45 IST overpass with an ERA5-Land skin-temperature heating rate. The correction (typically a few tenths of a degree, more for early Landsat 5 scenes) carries its own uncertainty, included in the level intervals.

Night LST is in Aqua-equivalent units: the 2025 frame is VIIRS and the 2000 frame Terra (22:30), both calibrated to Aqua on overlap years; 1990 and 1995 night frames are model hindcasts, not observations.
ERA5-Land climate covariates have ~9-11 km native resolution (bilinearly resampled to the grid) and known warm/dry biases over irrigated Indo-Gangetic cropland.
Land cover is GLC_FCS30D for every frame (five-yearly maps before 2000, ~81 % global accuracy); the 2025 frame uses its 2022 map.
GHSL built-up and population for 2025 and 2030 are model extrapolations (GHSL P2023A), and GHSL accuracy before 2000 is lower (Landsat back-casting).

Projections 2030-2050 are scenario projections, not forecasts: they combine CMIP6 temperature deltas scaled by an empirical dLST/dTair sensitivity with simulated land change, with Monte-Carlo uncertainty.
SHAP values explain the model's predictions, not causal effects; thresholds and recommendations are model-based what-if estimates.
District boundaries are APPROXIMATE (nearest-HQ Voronoi partition of the SPEC_v1 §1.2 outline): district names and per-district statistics describe approximate areas.
SYNTHETIC DATA: every variable is simulated from planted responses; see SYNTHETIC_TRUTH. No result describes the real Delhi NCR.
SYNTHETIC future inputs (34 pseudo-GCMs, SSP urban growth, population factors, GSAT increments) are illustrative stand-ins, not real scenario data.

SHAP values explain the model, not causal effects. Zone recommendations are model-based counterfactuals (the final model re-evaluated on the zone's cells after a feasible land-cover / NDVI / landscape change, with the neighbourhood (focal) features recomputed); the cooling they report is associated with the change in the model, not a causal effect.

Targets are per-frame anomalies (fixed-mask mean removed); absolute degC = anomaly + the frame level of section 09. Day levels are corrected to a 10:45 IST reference overpass; night is in Aqua-equivalent units.
Headline accuracy is pooled out-of-fold R2/RMSE under 20 km block cross-validation (spatial) and leave-one-epoch-out with recentred predictions (temporal); random CV is an optimistic upper bound.

Night 1990 and 1995 are model hindcasts (tier 'modelled', no satellite product exists); night 2000 is Terra 22:30 calibrated to Aqua (tier 'reconstructed'). Their intervals combine conformal model error and the level uncertainty.
In-browser scenarios use depth-6 surrogates of the final models (model_web_<mode>.json fidelity) and recompute the focal features on the grid (FOCAL_SPEC).
day: only 6 bootstrap replicates - intervals are a replicate range (bias-corrected 2.5-97.5 percentiles), not calibrated 95% confidence intervals.
night: only 6 bootstrap replicates - intervals are a replicate range (bias-corrected 2.5-97.5 percentiles), not calibrated 95% confidence intervals.

Frames 2030-2050 are a scenario projection, not a forecast: CMIP6 temperature deltas x an empirical dLST/dTair sensitivity + simulated land change, Monte-Carlo quantiles (GCM, sensitivity, land realisation, model error). SSP1-2.6 climate is pattern-scaled from SSP2-4.5.

day.block_size_source: block20 XGBoost OOF residual correlogram (< 0.1 beyond ~18 km)
day.ci_method_description: bias-corrected percentile interval: the 2.5/97.5 replicate percentiles shifted by (full-data estimate - replicate median); always contains the estimate

night.block_size_source: block20 XGBoost OOF residual correlogram (< 0.1 beyond ~18 km)
night.ci_method_description: bias-corrected percentile interval: the 2.5/97.5 replicate percentiles shifted by (full-data estimate - replicate median); always contains the estimate

formula.day: anom_day = -4.5*min(ndvi,0.30)/0.30 - 1.2*clip((box3km(ndvi)-0.20)/0.15,0,1) + 2.2*clip((ndvi_drop-0.12)/0.28,0,1) - 9.0*(albedo-0.18) - 2.2*built_f + 2.8*frac_barren - 7.0*(1-exp(-box1km(frac_water)/0.08)) - 0.8*exp(-dist_water/0.6km) - 12*(swvl1-mean) + 0.6*(vpd-mean) - 0.0045*(elev-220) + 0.006*tpi7km + noise; centred to 0 over the ROI at 1 km
formula.night: anom_night = 3.2*(1-exp(-built_f/0.30))/(1-exp(-1/0.30)) + 0.6*log1p(built_v) + 2.5*(1-exp(-box1km(frac_water)/0.08)) - 0.8*ndvi - 1.2*frac_barren + 0.012*tpi7km - 0.003*(elev-220) + 6*(swvl1-mean) - 0.4*(vpd-mean) + noise; centred to 0 over the ROI
formula.level: L(y) = base + trend*(y-2010)/10 + beta*(T(y)-T_ref) + gamma*(swvl1(y)-swvl1_ref); frame level = mean of L(y) over the frame window; T = era5_tmax (day) / era5_tmin (night)

synthetic_truth.level_definition: ROI mean (1 km cells) of the true absolute field; day at the 10:45 IST reference overpass in Landsat units, night in Aqua-equivalent units

uhi.definition: mean anomaly over cells with frac_built >= 0.5 minus cells with frac_built <= 0.05 and frac_water < 0.2 (SPEC §4.7)

overpass.note: RAW lst_day_f = truth - (10.75 - overpass_h) * heating_rate; SPEC §4.7 correction recovers the 10:45 IST truth

path_offsets.convention: per-path bias relative to the harmonised mosaic (value removed from that path's composite); planted symmetric +-delta/2 with delta = 146 - 147

terra_to_aqua.note: OLS on noisy source values attenuates b by var(true)/var(observed); expected_ols_b is the planted slope times that reliability

viirs_to_aqua.note: OLS on noisy source values attenuates b by var(true)/var(observed); expected_ols_b is the planted slope times that reliability

climate.gradient: SW -> NE: NE cooler by day, wetter (swvl1 0.11 -> 0.25), smaller diurnal range

future.note: synthetic stand-ins: pseudo-GCMs (not real CMIP6 output), Chen-2020-like urban ratios, IIASA-SSP-like population factors, AR6 Table 4.5 central GSAT values
